# Quill.Code - Shared instructions

**Single source for Claude and Copilot. Read first.**

---

## About the project

Quill.Code is a .NET library (NuGet packages) gathering the building blocks shared by the code editors of **Querify** (MAUI) and **PocketForge** (WPF): syntax highlighting, completion, diagnostics, hover, signature help and editing algorithms.

**Founding rule**: no dependency on a UI framework. No WPF, MAUI, `Brush`, framework `Color` or control. The library produces data (colored spans, suggestions, diagnostics); each application displays it.

---

## Architecture

`Quill.Code` ← `Quill.Code.[Language]` (one project per language). A language never references another language.

`Quill.Code.CSharp` ← `Quill.Code.CSharp.Linq` (C# in an EF context, not another language, engine-agnostic) ← `Quill.Code.CSharp.Linq.[Engine]` (one project per engine: `ILinqDatabaseProvider`; SqlServer, MySql, PostgreSql, Oracle, Sqlite).

SQL: `Quill.Code.Sql.SqlServer` is the T-SQL language (editor + SQL Server execution); the other engines have their `Quill.Code.Sql.[Engine]` project (MySql, PostgreSql, Oracle, Sqlite): execution only for now, on `DbQueryExecutor`. All of them reference `Quill.Code.Sql` (← `Quill.Code`), which holds the contract and the base of SQL execution.

`Quill.Data.Sql` ← `Quill.Data.Sql.[Engine]` (one project per engine, the only ones depending on a driver); `Quill.Data.Sql` ← `Quill.Code.Sql.SqlServer` and `Quill.Code.CSharp.Linq`. A `Quill.Code.*` never references a `Quill.Data.Sql.[Engine]`: the editor stays connection-free. Only the executors connect: `SqlServerQueryExecutor` (Microsoft.Data.SqlClient), the `[Engine]QueryExecutor` of `Quill.Code.Sql.[Engine]` (their driver) and `LinqQueryExecutor` (EF Core, through the engine's provider: `SqlServerLinqProvider`, `MySqlLinqProvider`…).

* **`Quill.Code`** (net8.0): models and contracts (`Completion`, `Analysis`, `Text`, `Scripting.LogLevel`), highlighting (`Highlighting`), editing (`Editing`), execution shared by languages (`Execution`: options, result sets, `QueryParameter` / `QueryParameterType` parameters; limits and timeouts in `Constants/QueryExecutionLimits`, shared by SQL and LINQ). No dependency.
* **`Quill.Code.Sql`** (net8.0): foundation of SQL execution (`Execution`): `ISqlQueryExecutor` contract; `DbQueryExecutor`, ADO.NET base of the engine executors — batches through `SplitScript` (a single one by default, `QueryBatch`), server messages through `AttachMessages`, command settings through `PrepareCommand`, parameter name, type and value, error text —; `DbResultSetReader`, reading a set into a `QueryResultSet`, shared with `SqlServerQueryExecutor`. No dependency (System.Data.Common is in the BCL).
* **`Quill.Code.CSharp`** (net8.0): C# via Roslyn. Public: `CSharpLanguageService`, `CSharpLanguageOptions`, `CSharpReferences` and, in `Compilation`, `CSharpCompileOptions`, `CSharpCompilationResult`, `CSharpRunAbandonedException`; everything else is internal.
  * `CSharpLanguageService(() => options)` is the only entry point: it owns its project (created on first request) and works directly on the editor text. `SourceTransform` gives the analyzed source, of the same length as the text (e.g. neutralized directives); `TextReferences` adds the references the text declares; `SetSource`/`SetSourceFileAsync`/`RemoveSource` add sources on the fly (applied on the next request, compiled with the text). Positions are always those of the editor text.
  * `Roslyn/` (internal): `RoslynHost` (single MEF composition, projects taken as snapshots of an empty solution: nothing to release), `CSharpProject` (sources on the fly, text references), `CSharpDocument`.
  * `Features/` (internal): one static engine per feature (`CSharpCompletionEngine`, `CSharpDiagnosticEngine`, `CSharpHoverEngine`, `CSharpSignatureHelpEngine`) on a `CSharpDocument`; the service calls them on the thread pool.
  * `Compilation/`: `CompileAsync` (emit, optional PDB, loading into a collectible context) and execution (`CSharpLanguageService.RunAsync`: compilation, entry point and unloading in one call, no return value — output through `CSharpCompileOptions.Log`, compilation failure thrown as `CSharpCompilationException`; or in two steps `CSharpCompilationResult.RunAsync` / `RunEntryPointAsync`: off the calling thread, abandoned on cancellation, unloaded when it actually ends — the calling contract stays with the application). Script runtime (`CSharpLanguageOptions.IncludeScriptRuntime`): `Log`, `LogLevel`, `Script` generated in each assembly and wired by reflection (`CSharpCompileOptions.Log`, `Script.CancellationToken`), hence specific to each execution and without any reference to the application.
* **`Quill.Code.Sql.SqlServer`** (net8.0, ScriptDom, Microsoft.Data.SqlClient): connection-free T-SQL. `SqlLexer` (tolerant of text being typed), `SqlContextAnalyzer` (static context: `Analyze(text, caret, database)` gives the expected kind, the qualifier, the tables/aliases of the current batch delimited by GO and the database of the last `USE`; `AnalyzeScope` for hover), `SqlSyntaxChecker` (ScriptDom `TSql170Parser`, names not checked) and `SqlLanguageService(SqlLanguageOptions)`, the only entry point: diagnostics, completion (static keywords `SqlKeywords`, catalog objects and columns depending on the context, document words, host variables) and hover (columns, tables, aliases, schemas, databases, declared or provided variables). `Schema/`: `ISqlCatalog` on the `Quill.Data.Sql` model, implemented by the host (Quill connects to nothing; an unavailable database is returned empty, an exception counts as a missing schema) or by the in-memory `SqlCatalog`. At the root, next to `SqlLanguageService`: `SqlServerQueryExecutor` (implements `ISqlQueryExecutor` from `Quill.Code`: connection string → `RunAsync` of a script, GO batches included, no return value: everything goes through `DataRunOptions`; `ReadAsync` of a parameterized query, errors thrown; Microsoft.Data.SqlClient, SSMS behavior). `SqlLanguageOptions.CheckSyntax` (false) turns off ScriptDom diagnostics for text in another dialect. `RunAsync(string, script, DataRunOptions?)` hands over PRINT (Information, `Code`), affected rows (Information, `Host`) and SQL errors (Error, following batches still run) through `Log`, each set through `Data`; cancellation throws `OperationCanceledException`. The displayed summary (duration, errors, cancellation) is up to the application. `Execution/`: `SqlBatchSplitter` (internal); parameters and limit come from `Quill.Code`. Per-feature services are internal.
* **`Quill.Code.CSharp.Linq`** (net10.0, EF Core Relational without an engine: EF Core 10 only targets net10.0): LINQ / EF queries in native C# (top-level statements) on a DbContext generated from a `SqlDatabaseSchema`, `Db` context, parameters usable by name (without @), data shown through `.Dump(title)`, `Log.*` from the script runtime. Public: `ILinqDatabaseProvider` (the engine: C# type of a column, EF provider assemblies added to the references, connection string, `Configure` of the context; one instance per application, compiled DbContexts and references being cached per provider), `LinqLanguageService(LinqLanguageOptions)` (editor: `Provider`, structure read again on each request through `Schema`; without a provider, null or exception = C# only; `Parameters`) and `LinqQueryExecutor(provider)`, modeled on `SqlServerQueryExecutor`: `RunAsync(string, structure, script, DataRunOptions?)` with no return value (context, generated SQL and rows read as Information/Host, `Log.*` as Code, compilation errors and script exceptions as Error/Code, each Dump through `Data`; cancellation thrown, `CSharpRunAbandonedException` if the script keeps running in the background) and `ReadAsync(string, database, structure, query, parameters, maxRows)` (last Dump, errors thrown as `InvalidOperationException`). Internal: `Modeling/` (`EfModelGenerator`), `Compilation/` (`LinqQuerySource`: frame generated around the query; `LinqCompiler`: model, `QueryGlobals` and queries, one `CSharpLanguageService` per `QueryGlobals`, shared by the editor and the execution; `LinqContexts`: cache provider + structure → compiled model and model + parameters → `QueryGlobals`, held by the structure, failures not kept), `Execution/` (`LinqParameter`, `LinqResultConverter`: value of a Dump → `QueryResultSet`).
* **`Quill.Code.CSharp.Linq.SqlServer`** (net10.0, EF Core SqlServer): `SqlServerLinqProvider(applicationName)`, the only public type: SQL Server types → C# (default EF Core mapping; `sql_variant`, `hierarchyid`… ignored), `UseSqlServer`, connection string through `SqlConnectionStringBuilder` (application name, database).
* **`Quill.Code.CSharp.Linq.[Engine]`** (net10.0): same shape, one public provider per engine. `MySqlLinqProvider(applicationName)` (Microting.EntityFrameworkCore.MySql, EF Core 10 fork of Pomelo: `tinyint(1)` → bool, sign read from `DataType`, server version detected once per server, schema ignored — it is the database), `PostgreSqlLinqProvider(applicationName)` (types through `pg_type.typname`), `OracleLinqProvider` (NUMBER(p,0) → integer according to p, 19c-compatible SQL, database ignored), `SqliteLinqProvider` (SQLite affinity, database ignored).
* **`Quill.Code.Sql.MySql` / `Quill.Code.Sql.PostgreSql` / `Quill.Code.Sql.Oracle` / `Quill.Code.Sql.Sqlite`** (net8.0, their driver: MySqlConnector, Npgsql, ODP.NET Core, Microsoft.Data.Sqlite): one public `[Engine]QueryExecutor` on `DbQueryExecutor`. MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite: script as one command (the driver chains the statements, an error stops the rest), server messages (InfoMessage, NOTICE) as Information/Code. Oracle: one statement per command, `Execution/OracleScriptSplitter` (internal) splits like SQL*Plus (`;` removed, PL/SQL block up to a `/` line), a failed statement does not stop the following ones; `:name` parameters bound by name, boolean as NUMBER(1), Guid as RAW(16).
* **`Quill.Data.Sql`** (net8.0, no dependency): structure of a database — `SqlDatabaseInfo`, `SqlDatabaseSchema` (index by name, `dbo` preferred), `SqlSchemaObject` (+ `Comment`), `SqlColumn` (displayed and system type, nullability, rank in the primary key, precision/scale, FK, identity, computed, comment, SSMS-style `Description`), `SqlSchemaObjectKind` — and the `ISqlSchemaReader` reading contract (databases, objects of a kind, columns of an object, complete schema in one round trip).
* **`Quill.Data.Sql.SqlServer`** (net8.0, Microsoft.Data.SqlClient): `SqlServerSchemaReader`, reads the `sys.*` views.
* **`Quill.Data.Sql.[Engine]`** (net8.0, the engine's driver): `MySqlSchemaReader` (`information_schema`; schema = database), `PostgreSqlSchemaReader` (`pg_catalog`; functions listed with procedures), `OracleSchemaReader` (`ALL_*` views; one database per connection, schemas = users not supplied by Oracle), `SqliteSchemaReader` (`sqlite_master`, `pragma_table_xinfo`; databases = main and attached databases, schema = database). Tolerant reading of catalog columns through `DbDataReaderExtensions` from `Quill.Data.Sql` (`GetFlag`, `GetInt32Value`, `GetByteValue`, `GetTrimmedStringOrNull`).
* **`Quill.Code.Tests`** (net10.0, xUnit).

Raw-text contracts in `Quill.Code` (`ICodeCompletion`, `ICodeDiagnostic`, `ICodeHover`, `ICodeSignature`, combined in `ICodeLanguageService`), implemented by `CSharpLanguageService` and `SqlLanguageService` (no language-specific interface: apps use the class for compilation and sources): an editor control binds to them without depending on Roslyn. An application's richer contracts (query with connection, language, parameters…) stay in the application and plug into Quill's engines.

What is specific to an application stays in the application: Querify's connections and structure cache (the same `SqlDatabaseSchema` instance gives the same compiled DbContext), PocketForge's NuGet directives and script entry point, specific `.xshd` files.

---

## Conventions

* **Reuse before creating**: before adding a class, an enum or a model, look for an existing type covering the need, from Quill first then from the project, even if it means extending it (an enum value, a property); only create a type if none fits, and in Quill, prefer a shared type (`Quill.Code`) over per-language variants (e.g. execution messages are Quill `LogEntry` items, not a dedicated model).
* **One type per file**, named after it. Only exception: a private nested class.
* **Execution messages** (`Quill.Code.Scripting`): timestamped `LogEntry(Level, Text, Source)` (`Timestamp`), received by `RunOptions.Log`; `LogLevel` is the severity (names and values of Microsoft.Extensions.Logging), `LogSource` the origin (`Host`: the executor; `Code`: a script's `Log.*`, PRINT and SQL errors of a batch); no other message model.
* **Execution options** (`Quill.Code.Execution`): `RunOptions` (`Log`, shared by every execution) ← `CSharpCompileOptions` (C# compilation and `RunAsync`) and ← `DataRunOptions` (`Log` + `Data`: each `QueryResultSet` handed over as soon as it is read; SQL, LINQ execution). Result sets (`QueryResultSet`, `QueryResultColumn`, `QueryResultRow`) and parameters (`QueryParameter`, `QueryParameterType`) are there too, shared by languages. Same contract for each executor: `RunAsync` with no return value (everything through `Log` and `Data`, code errors as Error without an exception, cancellation thrown), `ReadAsync` returns a set and throws its errors.
* **Constants**: never declared in a working class. Each project puts them in `Constants/` (namespace `<Project>.Constants`), one static class per context: `CodeLanguages`, `CompletionConstants`, `EditingConstants`, `HighlightingConstants`, `QueryExecutionLimits` (Quill.Code); `CSharpScriptConstants`, `CSharpDiagnosticConstants` (CSharp); `LinqQueryConstants`, `EfModelConstants`, `LinqExecutionConstants` (CSharp.Linq); `QueryResultConstants` (Code.Sql); `SqlAnalysisConstants`, `SqlServerConstants` (Code.Sql.SqlServer); `OracleScriptConstants` (Code.Sql.Oracle); `SqlSchemaConstants` (Data.Sql); `[Engine]Constants`, `[Engine]Queries` (Data.Sql.[Engine]). `internal` unless the constant is part of the API.
* **Instantiation**: no dependency injection in Quill (no container, no static registry, no `[AutoRegister]`). The rule only applies to the library: apps instantiate the services (`new CSharpLanguageService(() => options)`) or register them in their container through a factory; expensive work (MEF, references) is deferred to the first request.
* **Minimal public API**: `internal` by default, `public` only for what apps consume. `sealed` by default.
* **Async**: `CancellationToken` as the last parameter of every asynchronous method; the Roslyn workspace is never modified (projects and documents as snapshots), concurrent requests take no lock.
* **Package versions**: only in `src/Directory.Packages.props`, never a `Version` in a `PackageReference`.
* **Breaking changes**: recorded in `CHANGELOG.md`; major version from 1.0 on.

## Comments and language

* Everything in English: type and member names, XML documentation, code comments, README, CHANGELOG and commit messages.
* `/// <summary>` on every public member (documentation embedded in the package).
* Concise comments: the **why**, never the what.

## Commits

Format `type: description` in English (`feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `docs:`, `chore:`, `test:`).

No trailers in commit messages: no `Co-Authored-By`, `Claude-Session`, `Signed-off-by` or any other attribution line.

## Validation

```
dotnet build src/Quill.Code.slnx
dotnet test src/Quill.Code.slnx
```
